name: microsoft/presidio
what_it_is: Presidio is a Python SDK and set of REST microservices for detecting and anonymizing PII entities in unstructured text, structured/semi-structured data, and images. It ships four independent modules: Analyzer, Anonymizer, Image Redactor, and Structured.
components: presidio-analyzer: PII detection engine using NLP, regex, rule-based logic, and checksum recognizers
presidio-anonymizer: PII replacement engine supporting redact, replace, mask, hash, and encrypt operators; includes a deanonymizer
presidio-image-redactor: OCR-based PII redaction in raster images and DICOM medical images
presidio-structured: PII identification and anonymization in structured/semi-structured data
RecognizerRegistry: pluggable registry of PII recognizers
NlpEngine: swappable NLP backend (spaCy, Transformers, Stanza)
ContextAwareEnhancer: boosts confidence scores using surrounding word context
ollama: local LLM sidecar used by the analyzer for model-backed detection
protocols: HTTP REST (JSON payloads) for all three service endpoints
measurement: Per-entity confidence score (float 0-1) returned with every RecognizerResult
Entity type, start offset, and end offset for each detected span
configuration: Custom PII recognizers (regex patterns, deny lists, checksums, ML models)
NLP engine backend selection (spaCy, Transformers/HuggingFace, Stanza)
Anonymization operator per entity type (replace, mask, redact, hash, encrypt, custom)
Context words list for context-aware score enhancement
modes: HTTP microservice (Docker or native Python runtime)
constraints: Automated detection does not guarantee 100% recall; additional safeguards are required for compliance
Image redaction relies on OCR accuracy; degraded images may yield missed PII
Deanonymization is only possible for encryption-based operators; destructive operators (redact, hash) are irreversible
Language support depends on the underlying NLP model; not all entity types are available in all languages
DICOM support is limited to the image-redactor module; no native HL7/FHIR parsing
docker_services: ollama (port 11434, local LLM backend for analyzer)
notable_absences: No built-in audit log or decision trail for anonymization actions
No native HL7 or FHIR data parsing
No data-at-rest storage or database; stateless service only
No built-in synthetic data generation (de-identification only, not synthesis)
No UI dashboard; purely programmatic/API access
